uncited: This family extracts isosurfaces from scalar fields defined on non-Cartesian domains, including arbitrary polyhedral cells and hybrid unstructured grids, solving the topological inconsistencies and geometric discontinuities inherent in standard grid-based methods like Marching Cubes [951-isosurface-extraction-on-arbitrary-polyhedral-grids.md].

It sets itself apart by operating directly on complex cell geometries (such as pentahedra or arbitrary polyhedra) without requiring decomposition into tetrahedra or reliance on predefined configuration tables for ambiguous faces [951-isosurface-extraction-on-arbitrary-polyhedral-grids.md].

All methods in this family operate on a discretized domain, typically a regular grid (Cartesian, octree, or tetrahedral) where each cell contains scalar values or occupancy states at its vertices or centers.
**Surface Determination**: A criterion is applied to identify surface locations.
In isosurface methods, this involves comparing scalar values against a threshold (isovalue) to detect sign changes or equality [30-isosurface-extraction.md].
In blocky meshing, this involves checking occupancy states or material IDs to identify exposed boundaries [31-blocky-meshing.md].
**Mesh Coherence**: Adjacent primitives are merged or connected to form a coherent mesh, often requiring vertex merging to avoid duplicates and ensure watertightness [30-isosurface-extraction.md].

The need for methods handling arbitrary grids arises from the limitations of structured grid algorithms (like Marching Cubes) when applied to complex geometries or hybrid meshes common in engineering simulations.
